answer: Each agent may propose jobs, but payment comes only after a randomly selected set of established agents verifies the result against a public rubric; verifiers stake funds that are slashed if later audits find collusion or fabricated work. A new identity has no reputation or stake, so splitting one attacker into many accounts does not multiply influence: each still needs costly collateral and independently useful output. Like a river shaping a channel, repeated honest work builds trust over a long horizon, while attempts to forge evidence risk losing the stake.
